notes: 2026-07-29 nightly: NO strategy parameter changed on either engine -- live evidence is still n=1 closed trade, and last night's bucket analysis over 110 backtested S2 trades found no actionable gradient in stretch/ADX/RSI-depth. Tonight's work was an availability bug, and it was a serious one. THE FREEZE: the bot logged nothing between 2026-07-28 22:05 and 2026-07-29 02:07 UTC -- 4 hours -- while systemd reported it 'active (running)'. Both the main loop and the tracker thread were parked in wchan=wait_woken with no timer: a blocking socket read that could never return. ROOT CAUSE: hyperliquid.api.API defaults timeout=None and passes it straight to requests.post, so a half-open socket blocks forever. executor.py built Info/Exchange without a timeout and indicators.py built a fresh untimed Info on every candle fetch (20 coins x hourly = the most exposed surface). bot.log is full of 502s from the nginx in front of the API, which is exactly what produces half-open sockets. FIXES: (1) HTTP_TIMEOUT=(5,20) connect/read passed to every Info/Exchange in executor.py and indicators.py -- verified the value actually reaches the SDK objects, not just the constructor. (2) executor._hl_call now retries requests Timeout/ConnectionError with the same backoff it already used for 429/502/503/500, since that is the failure those timeouts now surface. (3) live.py gained a watchdog thread: the main loop calls _beat() every iteration, and if it goes silent past its allowance (900s normally, widened to 4800s around nightly_review because ai_brain runs to BRAIN_TIMEOUT=3600, 1800s around weekly_review and version_push) the watchdog logs, DMs the owner and os._exit(1)s so systemd (Restart=always, RestartSec=30) restarts it. Both directions tested in a subprocess: fires and exits 1 on a 20-min stall, and survives 75s of a healthy heartbeat without a false positive. (4) _release_lock() is now ownership-aware (only unlinks the pidfile if it still holds our own PID) so a dying instance cannot delete a newer one's lock. (5) review.py's _git() got timeout=120 -- git push talks to the network with no timeout, and a hang that reproduces nightly would have turned the new watchdog into a restart loop. COST OF THE FREEZE: 3 missed candle scans (23:00, 00:00, 01:00 -- 02:00 is quiet hours anyway) ~= 0.07 expected signals at the measured 0.53/day, plus the 23:00 UTC nightly review and its channel daily summary, which did not post on 07-28. Book was flat throughout, so no capital was at risk -- but S2 exits exclusively through its stop ratchet, so an open position would have had that ratchet frozen for 4 hours. DRIFT CHECK: re-ran the 20-coin S2 backtest with live ratchet semantics (partial_at_r=1.0, partial_pct=0.0, trail_step_r=0.25) -- C n=121 WR 66.1% +67.73%, B n=109 WR 64.2% +57.52%, A n=81 WR 65.4% +49.56%, quiet block n=12 WR 83.3% +10.21% maxDD -1.06%. Reproduces 07-28 within the rolling-window drift of the 5000-bar fetch. No drift in strategy2.py. The 02-04 quiet block is still the best measured block and is still paused by Mr G's standing rule -- his call.
